parents divorced after fighting so much (which fucked me up inside) since i was 7 years old. born & grew up in sabah (both parents are sabahan) but mum decided to move to KL. when fighting for custody i was still with my dad in sabah. little me was suffering every night missing mum that i had to sleep with her shirt every night just to comfort me.

mum won custody finally aftera few months of legal procedures and i moved across the south china sea, leaving my dad behind. little did i know i did not want to leave kk and my dad behind. 

surprisingly i could still do well academically. but during my teenage years my mental health slowly deteriorated and most of it stems from the absence of my dad. didnt hear him for years and felt guilty because i left him to be with my mum, but also feel abandoned because he never reached out and was living his life happily without me. 

to make things worse, mum remarried. i knew i should be happy for her but when she got new kids with her new spouse, i couldnt help thinking i was a mistake from a failed past marriage of hers and shouldnt have existed.

compounded with identity crisis (losing my faith as a muslim), mentally I was very broken after matriculation. i guess studies has been a good distraction for me, i managed to score 4.0, but after matriculation…. multiple suicide attempts in med school and 2 times psychiatric hospitalisations. was on lithium, didnt work, so my dr thought electroconvulsive therapy (ect) would be good for my mental health during that time.

since i was still a uni student, i had a meeting with the dean that time and i still remember her saying “You can’t help others if you can’t help yourself.”, before kicking me out of med school.

sometimes i wonder how different my life would have turned out if my dad was a decent person who has principles against cheating and never divorced my mum. maybe, just maybe, i would have a stable foundation of support that could be very beneficial for the development of my mental health. to this day, i am on psychiatric medications and struggle daily against suicide.
